articles.title: Podcast: Fire Prevention Tech to Protect Homes After LA Fires, CitroTech’s Wes Bolsen
articles.narrative: This article is a Q&A interview with Wes Bolsen, CEO of CitroTech, discussing the company's fire prevention technology and its implications for homebuilders and developers in fire-prone regions. Bolsen highlights the shift towards community-wide fire protection over individual home solutions, emphasizing the cost-effectiveness of prevention versus suppression. He also touches on how insurance companies are influencing construction practices and the potential for fire resilience to become a marketing differentiator for new homes, particularly in states like California, Colorado, Montana, and Idaho.

people.name: Wes Bolsen
people.title: Leadership team overseeing global wildfire prevention

articles.title: The Plan: The Metropolitan Museum of Art’s New Modern and Contemporary Wing Goes Big
articles.narrative: The Metropolitan Museum of Art has broken ground on the Oscar L. Tang and H.M. Agnes Hsu-Tang Wing, a new modern and contemporary art exhibition space at its 1000 Fifth Avenue location in Manhattan. The $670 million project, funded by private donors, will span 126,000 square feet across five stories and is designed by architect Frida Escobedo. The new wing is expected to open in 2030 and will double the museum's existing exhibition space for 20th- and 21st-century art.

data_points.property_name: Oscar L. Tang and H.M. Agnes Hsu-Tang Wing (The Metropolitan Museum of Art)
data_points.address: 1000 Fifth Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Features a limestone celosía facade, 69,500 square feet of exhibition space, over 18,500 square feet of outdoor terraces, and a 1,000-square-foot cafe. Designed with sustainability and accessibility in mind, including enhanced natural light and reduced solar gain.
data_points.project_notes: The project involves demolition and redevelopment of existing space. The Met is collaborating with the Central Park Conservancy and the New York City Department of Parks and Recreation on outdoor spaces.

articles.title: You Better Hope Suri Kasirer Takes Your Call
articles.narrative: This article profiles Suri Kasirer, founder of Kasirer, a prominent government relations firm in New York City. The firm has been the highest-grossing lobbying firm in the city for 17 of the past 20 years, playing a critical role in numerous significant real estate developments and rezonings, including One Vanderbilt and the 5 Times Square office-to-residential conversion. Beyond large-scale projects, Kasirer is deeply committed to working with nearly 50 nonprofits, driven by her personal history as the daughter of a Holocaust survivor and her experiences with financial uncertainty during her upbringing. Her philanthropic efforts include successfully advocating for legislation to ensure faster payments from city contracts to nonprofits.

articles.title: New York Investor Buys Palm Beach County Nursing Home for At Least $24M
articles.narrative: Tordjman Equities has acquired the Pine Trail Nursing and Rehab Center in Greenacres, FL, for at least $23.8 million. The 59,760-square-foot facility, built in 1988, features 93 beds and sits on an 8.7-acre property. The transaction was financed with a $150 million acquisition loan from Pinnacle Bank, which also backed another recent senior housing acquisition in Florida.

data_points.property_name: Pine Trail Nursing and Rehab Center
data_points.project_notes: The deed likely includes only the real estate value; the total price is probably higher to include the operating business and furniture. The asset last traded for $3.5 million in 2004.

articles.market_intelligence: Florida's senior population is projected to grow by 5.4 percent annually until 2031. Occupancy for senior housing properties in Palm Beach County held steady at about 90 percent in the second quarter of 2026.

articles.title: Bath & Body Works to Open 9K-SF Store in Flatiron District
articles.narrative: Bath & Body Works has signed a lease for a nearly 9,000-square-foot retail space at 129 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan's Flatiron District. The new store is expected to open in the fall of 2027, taking over a two-level retail unit previously occupied by another fashion retailer. This transaction marks a significant retail presence for the tenant in a prime New York City shopping corridor.

articles.title: Teeple Partners Breaks Ground on 312-Unit Multifamily Project in Bryan, Texas
articles.narrative: Teeple Partners has commenced construction on Oaks Reserve Apartments, a 312-unit multifamily development in Bryan, Texas. This project is the second phase of a larger 53-acre development that will ultimately comprise over 1,000 units. The first phase, Brazos Oaks, was completed earlier this year.

articles.title: MMCC Arranges $23.4M in Acquisition Financing for Travel Center in Mercedes, Texas
articles.narrative: Marcus & Millichap Capital Corp. (MMCC) has secured $23.4 million in acquisition financing for a 2,920-square-foot travel center in Mercedes, Texas. The 10-year loan, arranged by Ron Balys of MMCC, features a 6.75 percent interest rate and a 70 percent loan-to-value ratio. The financing was provided by an undisclosed national credit union for an undisclosed borrower.

articles.title: Partnership Buys 4.3-Acre Industrial Outdoor Storage Facility Near San Antonio Airport
articles.narrative: A partnership between Apricus Realty Capital and ABR Capital Partners has acquired a 4.3-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facility in San Antonio. The property, which was fully leased at the time of sale, is strategically located near San Antonio International Airport and offers specialized features including crane-served warehouse space and a concrete storage yard.

data_points.notable_features: Adjacent to San Antonio International Airport; features crane-served warehouse space, maintenance facilities, a concrete storage yard, and multiple drive-in loading positions.

articles.title: CanTex Capital Acquires 18,535 SF Industrial Building in New Braunfels, Texas
articles.narrative: CanTex Capital, a Dallas-based investment firm, has acquired an 18,535-square-foot industrial building in New Braunfels, Texas. The single-tenant property, completed in 2023, also offers industrial outdoor storage capabilities. The seller and sale price were not disclosed.

articles.title: Hyundai Transys to Invest $560M for Factory Expansion in West Point, Georgia
articles.narrative: Hyundai Transys Georgia Powertrain, an automotive parts manufacturer, is investing $560 million to expand its manufacturing operations in West Point, GA. The project involves upgrading two existing buildings and constructing a new third facility to increase production capacity for electrified powertrains for hybrid vehicles. This expansion is expected to create 320 new jobs.

data_points.notable_features: Expansion to support production of electrified powertrains for hybrid vehicles.

articles.title: Davis acquires two-building medical portfolio in Quad Cities area
articles.narrative: Davis has acquired a two-building outpatient medical portfolio totaling 51,856 square feet in the Quad Cities area for approximately $19 million. The Class A properties, located in Davenport, Iowa, and Silvis, Illinois, are fully leased to ORA Orthopedics under a new 15-year, triple-net master lease. This acquisition strengthens Davis' presence in the Midwest and aligns with its strategy of investing in high-quality medical properties with long-term tenancy.

data_points.notable_features: Class A outpatient medical portfolio occupied by a leading independent orthopedic and sports medicine practice.

articles.title: Former religious buildings could be blessing for multifamily investors
articles.narrative: This article explores the growing trend of converting former religious buildings into multifamily housing, highlighting their unique appeal to investors and cities seeking to expand housing options. These properties often boast established locations in dense neighborhoods, distinctive architecture that offers a competitive advantage in leasing, and a positive community reception due to preservation efforts. While presenting challenges such as unusual unit configurations and higher utility costs, experienced teams can mitigate these issues. The conversions contribute to the broader adaptive reuse movement, offering a sustainable way to add housing and expand the tax base without requiring new land.

articles.title: Draper and Kramer Incorporated purchases 268-unit multifamily building in Evanston
articles.narrative: Draper and Kramer, Incorporated has acquired Albion Evanston, a 268-unit luxury multifamily building in Evanston, Illinois. The 15-story property, which was 98.5% leased at the time of acquisition, will be rebranded as Eva and managed by Draper and Kramer. The acquisition provides the buyer with a well-occupied asset in a diverse market, appealing to both university affiliates and young professionals due to its amenities and transit access.

data_points.notable_features: The 15-story building features custom European-style cabinetry, quartz countertops, hardwood-style flooring, 9- to 11-foot concrete ceilings, floor-to-ceiling windows, in-unit laundry, and a range of hospitality-inspired amenities including a rooftop pool, fitness center, and coworking space. It also includes 7,090 square feet of fully leased first-floor retail space and 198 parking spaces.
data_points.project_notes: The property was 98.5% leased at the time of acquisition and will be rebranded as Eva under Draper and Kramer's ownership.

articles.title: Inflation Accelerates to 3.7% as Gasoline Prices Surge
articles.narrative: U.S. consumer prices saw an accelerated increase in September, with annual inflation reaching 3.7%, up from 3.4% in August. This surge was primarily driven by a significant 9.1% jump in gasoline prices, which accounted for over half of the monthly increase. Core inflation, excluding volatile food and energy components, also rose to 2.6% annually, suggesting broader inflationary pressures beyond just energy costs. Shelter costs continued their upward trend, contributing to the overall inflationary environment.

articles.title: Data Center Chip Market Set to Reach $1 Trillion by 2035
articles.narrative: A new report by DC Market Insights projects the global data center chip market to exceed $1 trillion by 2035, growing from $314.87 billion in 2025 at a CAGR of 12.49%. North America is leading this growth, driven significantly by AI accelerators, which constituted 53.9% of the market in 2025. The report highlights a structural shift where accelerators now hold more value than CPUs, memory, or networking individually, with custom in-house silicon expected to nearly double its market share by 2035 as hyperscalers increasingly design workload-specific chips.

articles.title: Marx Realty Secures Two Leases at 10 Grand Central
articles.narrative: Marx Realty has secured two new leases at 10 Grand Central, a hospitality-infused tower in the Grand Central neighborhood. Brenton Point will occupy 9,000 square feet on the 24th floor, and Cornerstone will take 5,000 square feet on the second floor. These leases underscore the building's appeal to a diverse range of companies seeking a high-quality, service-oriented environment with extensive amenities.

articles.title: RMR Lines Up $272M Mortgage Financing for Cedars-Sinai MOBs
articles.narrative: RMR Group Inc. has arranged $272.1 million in interest-only mortgage financing for two medical office buildings in Los Angeles, which are anchored by Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. The loan, provided by Morgan Stanley and BNP Paribas, has a two-year initial term with extension options and was used to refinance existing debt. The properties are owned by a joint venture, with Diversified Healthcare Trust holding a 20% equity interest.

data_points.address: 8631 and 8635 W. Third St., Los Angeles, CA
data_points.notable_features: Two 11-story medical office buildings connected to Cedars-Sinai Medical Center by skybridge, with two structured parking garages.
data_points.project_notes: Proceeds were used to repay approximately $267 million of existing mortgage debt scheduled to mature in February 2027 and to fund closing costs. The loan has a two-year initial term with three one-year extension options and bears interest at one-month Term SOFR plus 180 basis points.

articles.title: JLL Arranges $20M Sale of Fully Leased 107K-SF Retail Center in Ohio
articles.narrative: JLL Capital Markets has arranged the $20.55 million sale of Hilliard Rome Commons, a fully leased power center in Hilliard, Ohio. The property, which features a strong mix of national retailers and a separately parceled outparcel, was acquired by CASTO from seller RCG Ventures, LLC. Investors were attracted to the center's full occupancy, nationally recognized tenant lineup, and the flexibility offered by the outparcel.

data_points.notable_features: Power center anchored by national retailers, including a separately parceled outparcel.

articles.title: Charlotte City Council Leans Toward Extending Data Center Moratorium
articles.narrative: The Charlotte City Council is considering extending its existing 150-day moratorium on new data center developments by an additional 11 months. This potential extension follows a public hearing and precedes a scheduled vote on October 26, indicating ongoing deliberation regarding the future of data center growth within the city.

articles.title: Access To Power Now The No. 1 Force Shaping U.S. Site Selection Decisions
articles.narrative: Access to reliable and affordable electric power has become the paramount factor influencing site selection decisions for large-scale industrial projects, such as factories and data centers. This critical shift means that power availability now outweighs traditional considerations like government incentives and the local talent pool in determining where major developments are located.
articles.market_intelligence: Electric power has surpassed incentives and talent as the primary driver for megaproject site selection in the U.S.

articles.title: Wonderful Real Estate Inks Major Land Deals, Sells 1M SF Facility Near Bakersfield
articles.narrative: Wonderful Real Estate has completed the sale of a 120-acre parcel and a 1 million-square-foot logistics facility within its Central Valley logistics hub. The company also announced plans for future development at the site, indicating continued investment in the region's industrial market.

data_points.project_notes: The sale included both land and an existing facility at a logistics hub.

articles.title: South Florida Developers Pull Back On Industrial Construction
articles.narrative: South Florida's industrial construction pipeline has experienced a significant year-over-year decline, with new projects dropping by 42%. This pullback by developers indicates a notable shift in the region's industrial real estate market.
